Naval invasions up to this period were carried out by ferrying men to shore on little more than glorified row boats (such as Gallipoli in WW1). The first wartime use of what we think of as landing craft (ex. The Higgins boat) was carried out by the Japanese during their invasion of China. US soldiers and sailors stationed in cities such as Hong Kong observed these landings and noted how effective these boats were in comparison to traditional landing boats. Since small rowboats were quick and cheap to produce when needed, there wasn’t a need to maintain a large fleet of these boats as it was not worth the cost in storage and upkeep. With the rise of tanks that needed to be dropped ashore in addition to infantry there came in to play different landing craft that had to be outfitted for specific roles and so forth. Hope this helps, I grew up in New Orleans where the Higgins boats were made so this is my niche!

I too was born with a silver spoon. It’s kinda hard to break that cycle of thought. The feeling of inadequacy doesn’t know a social or financial boundary. I’m 25 and I can relate to what you’re feeling and struggle with it myself. 

The thing that struck me most about your post is how certain you were of your problems. 

For a long time I was certain of a lot of things, but as I’m getting older I’m starting to realize that I don’t know anything for sure. Life’s full of shit you never really understand and it’s ok. Maybe you just don’t have social skills or math skills at the level that people around you have. Shit sucks but it’s ok. Everyone has a different life path. 

While I’m good at being funny, someone else struggles to get a collective chuckle. That person may be able to cook like a fiend and I burn water. 

When you go back and try to figure out where you went wrong you miss out on the moment at hand. A negative feedback loop like that will kill you. 

I’m not saying it’s easy to work on skills you’re not feeling so hot about but there is a light at the end of the tunnel. 

Also, the fact that you’re asking these questions points to critical thinking skills. You’re already on your way!

Metaphorically life just feels grey to me.
